title: Car Loan Math: 72 vs 48 Months on a $35,000 Car
description:
A 72-month car loan makes the monthly payment look smaller, but you pay more in total. On a $35,000 car at an example 7% APR, 72 months costs about $7,963 in interest versus about $5,230 over 48 months: roughly $2,734 more for the same car. We also run the 20/4/10 rule of thumb.

Assumptions: $35,000 borrowed in full, 7% APR on both terms (an example; real rates depend on your credit and the lender, and longer loans can carry different rates), fixed monthly payments, no fees, taxes or add-ons. The 20/4/10 rule is a common guideline, not a law: put 20% down, borrow for 4 years or less, and keep car costs under 10% of gross income. The income figure uses the loan payment alone. Not financial advice.

scenes.say: A thirty-five thousand dollar car can cost you almost forty-three thousand. Here's how.
Take a seventy-two month loan at an example seven percent A-P-R. The payment looks friendly: about five hundred ninety-seven a month.
Over forty-eight months, it's about eight hundred thirty-eight.
But look at the interest. Seventy-two months: almost eight thousand dollars. Forty-eight months: about fifty-two hundred.
Same car, same rate. Two extra years of payments cost you over twenty-seven hundred dollars more.
A common guideline: twenty percent down, four years at most, and car costs under ten percent of your gross income.
For this car, that's a payment of about six hundred seventy a month. By that guide, you'd want to earn over eighty thousand dollars a year, before even counting insurance.
